Use sliding window for lossless internal pixel buffers

Replace full-height dec->pixels allocations with a sliding row
window bounded by the maximum VP8L backward-reference distance
and copy length. Size the window to the rows that must stay
resident across a shift instead of keeping a second copy.

Change-Id: I399190a7c195abc2c506ea53febca5db770a317f

use sliding window for decoded alpha rows

Allocate only a sliding output row window for dec->alpha_plane in
AllocateMemory (frame_dec.c) when alpha dithering is not active.
The row kept across a shift is the one still needed by unfiltering;
the shared window helper supplies the batch and copy headroom.

Change-Id: I2a32c3ed493f6e097e573cf5cf0de8a9c96fcfae

coupling: The overflow exists only when both window changes are present. VP8LGetWindowRows() (b519ff5) used to return twice the resident set (max_history_rows + NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS + ceil(MAX_LENGTH/width) headroom + 2) so a shift could amortize memmove. That commit now returns the resident set itself. With the alpha caller still passing max_history_rows=25, a 1024-wide image gets 48 rows, which is taller than this 32-row image and taller than FinishRow()'s last complex-filter batch, so the alpha plane is not a sliding window and the write stays in range. WebPGetAlphaWindowRows() (36b0cde) now passes max_history_rows=1, treating only the row before the batch as history and relying on VP8LGetWindowRows() to add the queued batch (NUM_ARGB_CACHE_ROWS is 16), the longest backward copy and the limit margin. Against the original doubled window that is still 48 rows, so this image is allocated in full and does not slide. Together, for width >= 1024, max_length_rows is 5 and the window is 1+16+5+2 = 24 rows. Height 32 is larger than 24, so dec->alpha_plane is a 24-row slice of the AllocateMemory() block. FinishRow() (frame_dec.c, unchanged by either commit) on the last macroblock row with the complex loop filter emits the 8 rows held back from the previous row plus all 16 rows of the last row (24) and keeps the preceding row, 25 rows in all. The uncompressed-alpha write of that batch (ALPHDecode -> NoneUnfilter) steps one row past the allocation. Restoring either the 2x factor or history=25 yields 48 rows, the 32-row image fits, and the PoC does not fire. Neither diff is locally inconsistent with the assumption written in that diff: the cache constant is 16, and the 24-row last flush lives only in FinishRow, which neither commit modifies. A fix has to reconcile the history argument with the undoubled window (or the window with the real 25-row flush); reverting only one of the two hunks removes the bug, and leaving either hunk as edited while restoring the other also removes it.
